issue.body:
This commit adds the X-Amz-Content-Sha256 header to all requests
as defined by the AWS documentation:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sig-v4-header-based-auth.html

Note, some SigV4 server implementations appear to strictly enforce this requirement while
others don't, which is why curl worked prior to this commit for some implementations
and not for others.

See Github Issue #8810

issue.title: --aws-sigv4 does not behave well with AWS VPC Lattice services

repository.name: curl
repository.description: A command line tool and library for transferring data with URL syntax, supporting DICT, FILE, FTP, FTPS, GOPHER, GOPHERS, HTTP, HTTPS, IMAP, IMAPS, LDAP, LDAPS, MQTT, POP3, POP3S, RTMP, RTMPS, RTSP, SCP, SFTP, SMB, SMBS, SMTP, SMTPS, TELNET, TFTP, WS and WSS. libcurl offers a myriad of powerful features

issue.body:
### I did this

Downloaded curl curl-8.0.1, patched like:

```
~/environment/curl-8.0.1 $ diff lib/http_aws_sigv4.c*
350c350
<   if(false) {
---
>   if(empty_payload || post_payload) {
488c488
<                 strcasecompare(service, "vpc-lattice-svcs"));
---
>                 strcasecompare(service, "s3"));
```

So I could run:

```
$ ./src/curl --aws-sigv4 "aws:amz:eu-west-1:vpc-lattice-svcs" --user "${ACCESS_KEY_ID}:${SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}" -H "x-amz-security-token: $SESSION_TOKEN" http://helloworld-XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX.vpc-lattice-svcs.eu-west-1.on.aws/hello 
yes this is patrick
```

### I expected the following

Same thing without the patch :)

### curl/libcurl version

```
$ ./src/curl -V
curl 8.0.1 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.0.1 OpenSSL/1.0.2k-fips zlib/1.2.7
Release-Date: 2023-03-20
Protocols: dict file ftp ftps gopher gophers http https imap imaps mqtt pop3 pop3s rtsp smb smbs smtp smtps telnet tftp
Features: alt-svc AsynchDNS HSTS HTTPS-proxy IPv6 Largefile libz NTLM NTLM_WB SSL threadsafe UnixSockets
```

### operating system

```
$ uname -a
Linux xxxxxxxxxx 4.14.311-233.529.amzn2.x86_64 #1 SMP Thu Mar 23 09:54:12 UTC 2023 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

### More details

Our of the box, a `curl --aws-sigv4 "aws:amz:eu-west-1:vpc-lattice-svcs" --user "${ACCESS_KEY_ID}:${SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}" -H "x-amz-security-token: $SESSION_TOKEN" http://helloworld-XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX.vpc-lattice-svcs.eu-west-1.on.aws/hello` gave me the following error:

```
IncompleteSignatureException: Missing the 'x-amz-content-sha256' in canonical headers
```

Upon reading https://github.com/curl/curl/pull/8935#issuecomment-1329440791, I modified just the `strcasecompare` so vpc-lattice-svcs would get the same logic for signature than s3. It was not enough, as `curl` gave me `InvalidSignatureException: Signed payloads are not supported` (which is correct [according to this service's documentation: "VPC Lattice does not support payload signing, therefore you must send x-amz-content-sha256 header with value set to "UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD"."](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc-lattice/latest/ug/sigv4-authenticated-requests.html)), hence my dirty bypass with the `if(false)` to the payload signing block. 

Relates to #8810 #8935
